decisions.rationale: Farigiraf denies priority and can reverse Whimsicott Tailwind with Mental Herb protection, while Heliolisk immediately pressures every Water lead through Dry Skin. Floette supplies the preferred Mega rain endgame and Palafin offers strong cleanup after a safe Flip Turn activation.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 preview plan: lead Farigiraf + Heliolisk into likely Whimsicott/rain pressure; Farigiraf’s Armor Tail blocks Aqua Jet and Mental Herb supports Trick Room through Taunt. Preserve Floette as preferred Mega versus rain and Palafin for Zero to Hero cleanup. Opponent roster: Whimsicott, Mega Blastoise, Politoed, Aqua Tauros, Maushold, Gholdengo; likely speed-control tools are Prankster Tailwind/Encore/Taunt, Icy Wind, and redirection.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott and Mega Blastoise establish immediate priority Tailwind and strong spread pressure, while Politoed provides Drizzle on entry for Water Spout and Tauros-Aqua. Tauros adds Intimidate and Close Combat pressure into Mawile and other physical threats; this four-Pokémon core preserves speed control and rain offense.
decisions.notebook: Preferred Game 1 composition is Whimsicott + Blastoise lead with Politoed and Tauros-Aqua in back: prioritize Tailwind and rain-boosted Water Spout, while using Tauros Intimidate and Close Combat against physical/Fairy threats. Farigiraf's Armor Tail can suppress priority disruption while active, so avoid relying exclusively on Prankster Taunt or Encore into it. Preserve Politoed when rain will decide Water Spout damage; consider Maushold or Gholdengo as alternate selections in later games if redirection or stronger anti-Fairy/Ghost pressure is needed.

selection: Trick Room (all adjacent, including ally Heliolisk)

decisions.notebook: Game 1 plan confirmed: prioritize Trick Room with Armor Tail + Mental Herb versus Whimsicott disruption; preserve Heliolisk through likely Mega Blastoise Aura Sphere, then leverage its Expert Belt Thunderbolt under Trick Room. Mega Blastoise Water Spout into exact Farigiraf is 41–58.1% at full HP as a spread hit; Heliolisk Thunderbolt into Mega Blastoise is 65.6–113.6%, not a guaranteed OHKO. Floette remains preferred Mega into rain; Palafin remains Zero to Hero cleanup.

reflections.summary: Won by reversing Whimsicott Tailwind with Trick Room, then using Helping Hand Thunderbolt to remove Mega Blastoise. Heliolisk remained an excellent rain endgame answer, while Mega Floette and Palafin covered the remaining Water/Fighting pressure. The four brought and Mega Floette were well suited to the revealed composition.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the Farigiraf/Heliolisk/Floette/Palafin framework, but prioritize eliminating or heavily pressuring Whimsicott sooner after Blastoise falls; its repeated Encore created unnecessary Heliolisk constraints. Continue Mega Evolving Floette unless the unrevealed back proves a different Mega plan is needed.
reflections.notebook: Opponent led Whimsicott + Mega Blastoise and brought Politoed + Aqua Tauros; Maushold or Gholdengo was omitted. Whimsicott reliably opens Tailwind and repeatedly uses Encore, with Taunt available. Politoed is a Damp Rock rain setter that repeatedly Protects and can use Icy Wind/Helping Hand. Mega Blastoise showed Aura Sphere and Dark Pulse coverage. Preserve Heliolisk for rain endgames; Farigiraf Trick Room effectively punishes Tailwind. Plan to pressure Whimsicott once Blastoise is handled, and retain Mega Floette as the default endgame Mega.

reflections.summary: Lost because the team-preview plan paired rain and Mega Blastoise into Dry Skin Heliolisk, giving the opponent a reliable super-effective target while Farigiraf established Trick Room. The chosen four lacked sustained pressure on Heliolisk, and Mega Blastoise was a poor Mega holder for this matchup.
reflections.adjustment: Change the four and Mega plan: do not bring Politoed/Mega Blastoise as the core into this opponent; use a different Mega holder or no Mega, and include a direct Heliolisk answer while prioritizing Heliolisk before it can repeatedly fire Thunderbolt.
reflections.notebook: Opponent's core plan is Farigiraf Trick Room plus early Heliolisk protection, followed by repeated Expert Belt Thunderbolt pressure; Farigiraf carries Mental Herb, so immediate Taunt is unreliable. Heliolisk's Dry Skin makes rain and Water-based damage poor into it, and Encore can lock it into Thunderbolt when reapplied. Mega Floette provides strong Fairy Aura pressure and uses Energy Ball to punish Politoed. Future games: avoid a Politoed/Mega Blastoise rain core, do not select Mega Blastoise as the default Mega here, bring direct Heliolisk counterplay, and account for Trick Room despite Farigiraf's Mental Herb.
